title: Stable Long-Range Charging and Boundary-Mediated Thresholds in a Waveguide Quantum Battery
authors: Li-Hong Yu, Zhuo-Yu Zhang, Yu Wang, Xin Li
abstract: The waveguide-integrated architecture holds promise for scalable on-chip integration of a charger, a transmission channel, and a quantum battery in a modular, independently optimizable design. We investigate a minimal charging configuration consisting of two emitters coupled to a semi-infinite waveguide and identify the optimal charging mechanism, wherein non-Markovian dynamics driven by out-of-band bound states give rise to single-frequency oscillations of the stored energy. We show that near-unity charging efficiency is achievable at weak to moderate coupling strengths via detuning control, provided that the battery-to-boundary separation $n$ is less than three times the charger-to-boundary separation $m$ ($n<3m$)---a constraint imposed by the mirror-induced feedback---while the average charging power decays exponentially with the spatial separation $n-m$. These findings offer useful insights for monolithic solid-state quantum energy storage and transport.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes energy storage and transfer in a quantum battery coupled to a waveguide. By solving the system dynamics using complex analysis techniques, the authors determine the conditions necessary for efficient, long-range charging. The results provide crucial guidelines for designing solid-state quantum energy storage devices.
main_problem: The paper investigates the feasibility and mechanisms for achieving stable, long-range energy charging in a quantum battery setup mediated by a waveguide.
main_result: Near-unity charging efficiency is possible under specific geometric constraints ($n < 3m$), and the average charging power decays exponentially with the spatial separation between the charger and battery.
method: The dynamics are solved by deriving coupled integro-differential equations, transforming them using the Laplace transform, and analyzing the residues of the resulting complex integrals.
model_or_system: The system models two emitters (Quantum Charger and Quantum Battery) coupled to a semi-infinite 1D Coupled-Resonator Waveguide (CRW) terminated by a mirror. The Hamiltonian includes terms for the emitters, the waveguide, and their respective couplings.
key_observables: Instantaneous stored energy of the QB, average charging power, and the time-dependent amplitudes of the coupled emitters.
important_parameters: Detuning ($\omega$), coupling strength ($\lambda$), and the spatial separations ($m$ and $n$) between the emitters and the boundary.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the CRW has open boundary conditions, and the long-time dynamics are governed by the poles (bound states) in the complex frequency plane.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup (QC, QB, CRW) and show the time evolution of the stored energy $E_B(t)$ under varying coupling strengths and detunings.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by defining the Hamiltonian and system dynamics, deriving the governing equations, solving them using Laplace transforms and contour integration techniques, and finally analyzing the long-time behavior dictated by the poles (bound states) to determine optimal charging regimes.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems dynamics, specifically energy transfer and coherent coupling in engineered photonic structures, which is central to modern quantum optics and cavity QED.
